document_summary: City of Santa Ana news release (posted March 5, 2026) describing a new ordinance banning algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rentals in Santa Ana, CA.

rules.title: Santa Ana ban on algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental properties in Santa Ana. Tenants may sue directly and need only prove the landlord used the prohibited technology, not intentional collusion.
rules.key_value: Ban on sale, licensing, provision and use of algorithmic rent-setting software using nonpublic competitor data
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits.
rules.exemptions: Pricing software relying solely on publicly available data or aggregate historical data, and tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements.
rules.interaction: Structured to operate alongside existing and proposed state antitrust laws while providing stronger local protections.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Municipal Code (ordinance number not stated in source)
rules.quoted_span: The ordinance, which was approved on March 3, 2026 for a second reading and final vote, prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental properties.
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary press release. Source says the ordinance was approved March 3, 2026 for second reading and final vote, so the final adoption date and effective date are not stated; both left null. Status in_force is inferred from the release's wording that the council passed the ordinance and the query date of 2026-10-01. Remedies (injunctive relief, damages, civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation plus attorney's fees) are not the key value.
